description:
STEP 2 (re-key on the arrow). Code-review finding 3. convergence_class / dispatch_mask keying is LOAD-BEARING fz-y6w bounded-specialization control -- NOT alpha-normalization -- and the dispatch KEY is deliberately distinct from precise input EVIDENCE (world_test.rs:222). Do not lose this when re-keying.

Today canonical_activation_key (world.rs:2709) applies convergence_class(input) per masked recursive slot to widen recursive non-dispatch slots (list(int) -> list(any)) so specialization stays bounded. Re-express this as a single WHOLE-ARROW operation at the mint:
  key = convergence_collapse(arrow, dispatch_mask)
operating on the interned arrow (one op, not per-input), preserving: (i) recursive non-dispatch slots widen to their convergence class; (ii) the key is a DERIVED collapse, the arrow remains the precise evidence surface (ActivationKey keeps both: arrow = evidence, key = collapse). Key != evidence is intentional.

Depends on: re-key ActivationKey (fz-hwn.27.6).
Checks: fz-y6w bounded-specialization tests stay green (e.g. quicksort spec count does not regress); world_test.rs:222 key-vs-evidence intent preserved; recursive slot widening still occurs. Lib + matrix green, zero warnings.

comments.text: Co-landing: not separable from 27.6. The convergence widening already lives inside canonical_activation_key (per-masked-slot convergence_class before normalization); it must become a whole-arrow convergence_collapse in the SAME commit that switches normalization to whole-scope addressing. See 27.6 finding.

title: key = convergence_collapse(arrow, dispatch_mask): preserve fz-y6w bounded specialization & key-vs-evidence split
